item.title: Meta heads to court in a landmark trial about kids and social media addiction
item.description: Four states are suing the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, alleging that the platforms were designed to hook kids and that Meta hid the mental health risks.
item.content:encoded:
Four states are suing the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, alleging that the platforms were designed to hook kids and that Meta hid the mental health risks.

item.title: Missed shifts were costly to this McDonald's. An app has fixed the problem
item.description: Unexpected absences can cost employers tens of thousands of dollars a month. An app that helps workers with last-minute transportation, food and childcare is making a difference.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: NPR's Michel Martin speaks with Fortune Magazine AI reporter Beatrice Nolan about the invisible watermark embedded in anything new models of Anthropic's AI assistant Claude processes.

item.title: Are robotaxis finally here?
item.description: Fully self-driving cars for hire have been hailed as the technology of the future for years now. That future has finally arrived -- but only in some cities.
item.content:encoded: Fully self-driving cars for hire have been hailed as the technology of the future for years now. That future has finally arrived -- but only in some cities.

item.title: Trump administration wants to allow companies to hack foreign cybercriminals
item.description: The White House memorandum is thin on details, but it aims to give private businesses the ability to sabotage or spy on certain foreign actors.

item.title: Recent AI 'escapes' are a warning of how unpredictable the technology can be
item.description: Recent episodes of AI agents escaping test zones and hacking other systems may be a harbinger of what's to come, as some experts believe the systems are fundamentally unpredictable.
